composition.observation: The companion holds the released passage in a centered reading panel beneath compact shell controls. The library changes to catalog layout, and the return restores the Journal and its tools.

hierarchy.observation: The companion leads with the active Voyage and Journal companion headings. The library leads with My Chronicle Library and Active Voyages, and the gold Continue Adventure control becomes distinct on the current card when it scrolls fully into view.

typography.observation: Serif titles separate the library, Voyage, and passage from compact sans-serif navigation. Dark type on parchment keeps the current passage legible across companion and returned Journal.

spacing.observation: The exit link uses a discrete contextual strip. The companion gives the reading-size buttons space above the passage. At 900 px high, the library card action takes a scroll from initial arrival.

controls.observation: Exit to My Voyages is a distinct contextual link. Continue Adventure is the gold primary card action, visually separate from Continue Solo and Pin to top. The returned reduced Journal shows replay and reading-size controls.

contrast.observation: Parchment against dark teal separates content from navigation. The gold continuation action and pale keyboard focus outlines are recognizable against the dark library.

consistency.observation: Both motion modes retain the same companion and catalog content. The teal shell, synthetic account witness, Voyage title, and Follow the lanterns stay recognizable across the compact and standard shell layouts.

states.observation: The Companion shows the released passage, the Library shows the active Voyage, and both returns restore the Journal. The normal returned screenshot shows the open spread, while reduced shows the intentional readable page-turn fallback.

responsive.observation: At the contract's 1440 by 900 desktop size, the compact shell, companion panel, library filters, and Journal tabs fit across the viewport in both modes. The library action is accessible through vertical scrolling.

keyboard.observation: Both traces show Tab navigation to the contextual exit and the library's Continue Adventure action. Enter on each link performs the destination change in both playback modes.

focus.observation: The trace shows visual focus moving through compact shell and library controls. The library heading acquires a visible outline after the exit, and tabbing to the adventure action brings its card into view.

feedback.observation: The library transition measures 130 ms normal and 100 ms reduced. Journal tools follow Continue Adventure at about 2.35 s normal and 0.49 s reduced. Both traces reach the terminal Journal-ready state.

motion.observation: The normal recording moves from the closed cover to the spread and removes the ceremony controls after settling. The terminal trace witnesses completed. Reduced lands on the intentional readable fallback and reports completed-fallback.

continuity.observation: The registered account witness matches at the companion, library, and return. The library card keeps the same Voyage title, and both traces verify the exact same-Voyage Journal path with the current passage.

complexity.observation: Two destination-labeled links complete the tested journey. The immersive companion suppresses the global menu, leaving the contextual library link in its own strip and the standard library exposing its expected navigation and filters.

role-outcomes.observation: The captured authorized Player registers the device, gets the released Journal companion, sees the active adventure in their own library, and reaches the same returning Journal with the replay control present.

fallbacks.observation: The contextual Library exit and same-Voyage re-entry remain usable in both modes. The reduced trace confirms the intentional readable fallback. Camera-unavailable Guided Lens and disabled companion purposes are outside this shell capture.

findings.observation: At the captured desktop height, the initial Library state places Continue Adventure below the fold despite a single active record. Keyboard focus scrolls the full card and its gold action into view, and the recorded journey completes.

On normal return, the already-readable spread remains beneath a settling ceremony before Journal tools appear about 2.65 seconds after Continue Adventure. A persistent opening-could-not-finish notice replaces the ceremony. The normal trace reports failure and phase-timeout. The same Voyage and page turning are available through recovery, but the normal opening does not complete successfully.
findings.resolution: In the fresh normal capture, Continue Adventure reaches visible Journal tools in about 2.35 seconds. The terminal trace reports JOURNAL_READY with completed outcome and completed reason. The actual recording shows the ceremony overlay clear and leave the readable spread without the previous failure banner. Reduced reports completed-fallback.

composition.observation: The Studio uses a centered two-by-two choice grid at desktop and a single-column mobile stack. Selecting manual opens the editor, with Details inline above the passage workspace.

hierarchy.observation: The large Create a Chronicle heading leads into the options. A gold treatment emphasizes the manual action and later the Save details action, with the draft title retained in the editor.

typography.observation: Serif Studio and creation headings establish the page hierarchy. Card titles are heavier than their descriptions, and metadata labels and the Saved at line stay legible at the mobile width.

spacing.observation: The desktop grid keeps distinct gutters and the mobile stack separates each card. Inline Details keeps the primary button beneath its fields with enough clearance above the passage library.

controls.observation: Create Manually opens the blank editor. The tested rename, Apply title, Chronicle Details, Save details and Close actions are inline controls with visually distinct active states.

contrast.observation: Cream heading text and the gold Save details mark the main actions on teal. Disabled alternatives remain readable in the choice grid despite lower emphasis.

consistency.observation: The Studio shell, account control and teal-and-gold visual language remain in the library, chooser and editor. Both browser sizes reach the same choices and real editor.

states.observation: The recordings show choices, untitled editing, inline Details and a named draft in the Library after Save. The first desktop run starts from an empty Library and makes the newly created card distinct.

responsive.observation: The desktop editor uses multiple columns. Mobile stacks the authoring content and preserves the Save action and its status in normal and reduced captures. The mobile choice stack naturally requires vertical scrolling.

keyboard.observation: The trace records Enter on the library entry, manual creation, rename, apply, open Details, save and close. Desktop and mobile captures show visible focus. The journey uses the named Close action, so it offers no direct Escape-path evidence.

focus.observation: The chooser and editor headings receive clear landing outlines. Keyboard movement in the records brings the target into view, and the Library heading gains focus when leaving the editor.

feedback.observation: Journey feedback ranged from 82 to 210 ms across the four contexts. The desktop normal trace shows the Saved at message within about 56 ms of Save details activation. Mobile retains the same adjacent confirmation without leaving the editor.

motion.observation: Normal and reduced playback show a restrained chooser-to-editor transition, then immediate inline authoring and save feedback. Both paths return to the Studio library and repeat the chooser entry.

continuity.observation: The first desktop recording starts with no Chronicles, enters and names Untitled Chronicle, then returns to a single card with the entered title and description. Subsequent captures share a fixture and display multiple identically named drafts, so title alone cannot uniquely identify them.

complexity.observation: The initial choice offers one previewable manual workflow, going straight into the editor without a metadata step. Details and save remain in the authoring surface. A return link reaches the Studio Library.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator reaches the actual draft Passage editor, changes title and short description, saves, and sees the draft card in the authenticated Library. The capture does not traverse every editable metadata field.

fallbacks.observation: The blank-editor path works without AI, import or a template. The desktop reduced recording shows the other three cards marked Coming soon and leaves manual creation as the available route.

composition.observation: A centered dark dialog separates the parchment clue from the dimmed Journal. Mobile uses a nearly full-height bounded sheet while keeping the clue and close button in the initial view.

hierarchy.observation: The dialog title and same Voyage context precede an availability line and the Guided View. The Captain’s note is the high-contrast task surface containing the clue and its actions.

typography.observation: The narrative title and clue use serif type, separated from the sans-serif control labels and availability explanation. The northern-light clue stays readable on the narrow capture.

spacing.observation: The desktop panel gives the clue and action strip a separate block. Mobile wraps the third action to a second row and keeps the inspection acknowledgement inside the note card.

controls.observation: The Journal Lens button opens the dialog. Inspect changes the clue card’s visible state. The top-right close control returns to the same Journal and its original Lens control.

contrast.observation: Dark text on parchment makes the released clue stand out. A gold outline marks the Close button and returned Lens opener against their teal controls.

consistency.observation: The same clue, Guided View structure and visible inspection response persist across both viewports and motion modes. Both normal-mode Journal states retain the live readable book without the prior opening failure notice.

states.observation: Each capture reaches Journal, then Lens with released note, then the changed inspection message and the same Journal after close. Normal entry ends completed in both traces and reduced entry ends completed-fallback.

responsive.observation: The desktop modal retains context around it while the compact mobile Lens label and tall modal preserve clue, Inspect and close. A mobile footer extends beyond this initial screenshot while the task actions remain visible.

keyboard.observation: The traces show Enter on Open Chronicle Lens, Inspect and Close on both sizes. The capture receipts verify keyboard traversal and visible focus across the tested steps.

focus.observation: Opening the dialog places a clear outline on the top-right close button. After closing, the same outline returns to the Journal's Lens control on both desktop and mobile.

feedback.observation: Boundary feedback ranged from 104 to 189 ms in the four captures. The desktop normal trace shows the changed note state within about 34 ms of Inspect activation. Both normal traces next expose Journal tools immediately after the dialog closes.

motion.observation: The normal Journal completes its settling transition on both browser sizes, and the open, inspect and close sequence leaves the passage readable. Both normal traces report completed, while reduced shows the intended readable fallback and reports completed-fallback.

continuity.observation: The clue and matching Voyage name stay visible through the dialog. Exact Journey traces and receipt verify matching Voyage and edition witnesses before, at outcomes and after return. The recordings show no cross-device handoff in this single-context consumer journey.

complexity.observation: The journey adds three distinct controls to the Journal task: open Lens, Inspect, and Close. The unavailable camera option explains why it is disabled and leaves Guided View immediately usable.

role-outcomes.observation: An authorized Player reads the real published clue, sees a changed inspection state on The Captain’s note, and returns to the same Journal. The evidence does not cover Creator-side publication, native camera operation or a paired-device handoff.

fallbacks.observation: Browser world tracking is explicitly unavailable in these captures. The full released northern-light clue, Inspect response, and contextual close remain usable with Guided View in both desktop and mobile. Unavailable companion purpose states are outside this Lens capture.

findings.observation: Both normal-mode viewports enter BOOK_SETTLING and end in JOURNAL_READY with opening failure and phase-timeout. The opening-could-not-finish notice is visible before Lens and remains on return. The camera-free clue, Inspect, close and same-Voyage continuity all work. The persistent unexpected fallback signals that the normal Journal opening did not complete.
findings.resolution: Both current normal traces reach JOURNAL_READY with completed outcome and completed reason, and both actual recordings show the ceremony clear without the timeout notice before Lens and after close. The same Voyage and edition, released clue, Inspect change and keyboard return remain intact. Reduced traces reach their intended completed-fallback.

composition.observation: The companion stacks a contextual exit, a Voyage purpose card and a distinct parchment reading panel in one column. The ordinary Library switches to a single column of search, filters and active cards. The Journal return keeps the parchment separate from the persistent chapter tools and objective button.

hierarchy.observation: Exit to My Voyages is a compact dedicated navigation row above the companion content. My Chronicle Library and Active Voyages establish where the Player has landed. The voyage card’s amber Continue Adventure and the returned Journal’s amber Continue Voyage give each step a clear next action.

typography.observation: The Library heading wraps at a word boundary across two lines. The companion and returned Journal use the larger serif Follow the lanterns title and smaller readable passage copy, while compact status and input labels use sans serif. The returned Journal’s compact chrome is denser than its parchment.

spacing.observation: The companion purpose card, released passage selector and reading-size controls have visible separation. Library filters use distinct stacked rows and the active card begins below them, so the Player scrolls to its action. The returned Journal leaves the fixed chapter tools and Continue Voyage strip in separate rows.

controls.observation: The companion exit, Library Continue Adventure and Journal Continue Voyage each have distinct text. After the Library card action, the trace resolves Replay full opening and Journal tools. The final button passes a viewport hit test and trial click in both modes.

contrast.observation: Light labels on dark teal identify the exit and navigation, brown passage text stands out against parchment, and the dark continuation labels stand out on amber. White visible focus indicators remain discernible over the Library background and controls. The state audits report no serious axe violations.

consistency.observation: Voyagewright dark shell and the CS identity badge carry across companion, Library and returned Journal. Parchment and serif treatment visually relate the companion excerpt to the restored passage. Normal and reduced screenshots retain recognizable purpose and action names.

states.observation: Journal companion shows a released passage and Same Voyage · in sync. The Library shows Server confirmed and an active Voyage. On return the Player sees Follow the lanterns, Journal tools and an unobscured Continue Voyage button. Normal settles into the Journal and reduced uses its readable page-turn fallback.

responsive.observation: On the MOBILE viewport, the Library title wraps and the Gallery/List controls and filter rows remain in one column. The Library card is reached by vertical scrolling. Both Journal action strips fit within the viewport; capture reports no document overflow in any of the three states in either mode.

keyboard.observation: Both trace sequences use Tab to reach the contextual exit and the Library’s Continue Adventure link, then Enter activates each. The final Continue Voyage has viewport hit testing and a successful trial click. Its state-changing activation is a separate local proof outside the archived journey.

focus.observation: The traces show outlines on the brand or Return controls while tabbing, the Library heading on route entry, and Library controls during the subsequent Tab sequence. Focus checks for the two navigation activations pass in both modes, and each action reaches the expected destination.

feedback.observation: Keyboard exit activation reaches the visible current Adventure outcome in the Library in 108 ms normal and 88 ms reduced against 5,000 ms. The subsequent Continue Adventure activation restores the current passage with a clear waiting or opening state in both modes.

motion.observation: The normal WebM shows the returning ceremony with Skip ceremony, then settles into Follow the lanterns with page controls and the objective strip. The previous opening failure banner is absent from the settled return. Reduced motion reaches the same passage and controls through its readable fallback.

continuity.observation: The companion, active card and Journal all show Synthetic Crossdeck refit Voyage. The companion and Journal show Follow the lanterns. The trace and capture independently bind the Journal URL ending in cd11/journal and equal authorized-person witnesses before exit, at the Library outcome and after return.

complexity.observation: The navigation task takes two purposeful decisions: exit the companion and continue the current adventure. The Library puts search and sorting before the active card, requiring a short vertical scroll, and the return offers chapter tools plus a separate primary objective action.

role-outcomes.observation: The authorized synthetic Player receives a released passage and the signed-in Library’s active adventure. The Library link restores that same Player’s Voyage Journal with the opening replay control, Journal tools and an unobscured Continue Voyage action in both modes.

fallbacks.observation: Reduced motion reaches the readable Journal fallback with the same active passage and safe return. The ordinary opening now settles without a failure banner in the recorded normal context. Guided Lens and paired behavior are covered by their own journeys.

findings.observation: Normal mobile return again displays an opening failure notice after the optional opening settles, while the readable passage, page navigation and Continue Voyage remain available. This can make a successful return feel uncertain. The same-Voyage destination and usable next action are preserved for this companion exit journey.
findings.resolution: In this capture normal mobile transitions from the opening ceremony to Follow the lanterns without the previous warning. The returned screenshot shows both page controls and Continue Voyage, and the trace confirms its button trial click.

composition.observation: On desktop the connection dialog sits centrally over a visibly retained parchment spread. On the handheld it becomes a narrow stacked panel, while the return restores the stable parchment and separate Journal tools and objective strip.

hierarchy.observation: Bring your phone aboard and the current Voyage title precede the QR and account instruction. The prominent QR carries the primary join instruction and Use a code instead offers an explicit alternate path. The unchanged Follow the lanterns heading anchors the return.

typography.observation: The pairing dialog uses a display heading and short readable lines for the account prompt. Mobile wraps the title without cutting words. The Journal uses a distinct serif passage heading and body against parchment; condensed utility labels occupy the darker chrome.

spacing.observation: The modal gives the QR a separate block from its directions and device list. The mobile list extends below the first screen, where Continue the Chronicle remains reachable by scrolling. The returned page's heading remains separated from the fixed Journal tools.

controls.observation: Connect another device opens the in-place dialog, which provides QR/code guidance and Continue the Chronicle. Both activation steps reach their destinations across viewport and motion settings. The paired phone receives the offered Chart through its visible Receive action.

contrast.observation: The black-on-white QR stands out against the dark dialog. Ivory and gold outlines identify the focus target and which control regained focus after dismissal. Brown passage text remains clear on parchment. Capture reports no serious axe issues for the recorded states.

consistency.observation: The Voyage name and parchment remain recognizable through modal opening and dismissal, and the same style holds across viewport and motion settings. Paired send and receive render the same nautical visual language, with distinct states for the sender and receiver.

states.observation: The traces include preparation before the QR appears, the ready dialog, and restored Journal. Paired cases show pending delivery, received Chart and sender acknowledgment. The adverse case refuses an expired code and removes the personal surface after revocation.

responsive.observation: Desktop retains a spread behind the dialog; handheld presentation stacks the QR and guidance and scrolls vertically. The 820-pixel paired Journal keeps a visible passage and objective strip. The 844-by-390 landscape companion frame shows its Chart heading only within the first viewport.

keyboard.observation: Trace events use Enter to activate Connect another device and Continue the Chronicle on desktop and mobile in both modes. They reach the dialog and return without requiring pointer input for the contextual navigation.

focus.observation: A clear ring surrounds the modal Close target on the handheld. On return a ring is visibly restored to Connect another device, preserving a reliable position in the Journal. The four isolated journey captures report passed focus checks.

feedback.observation: Keyboard activation to the contextual outcome takes 271–402 ms across the four isolated contexts. In the paired runs, send-to-offer is 414 and 497 ms and acceptance-to-acknowledgment is 465 and 554 ms. The phone visibly reaches the Chart and the sender moves from pending to acknowledged on both positive runs.

motion.observation: Both motion settings reach the QR dialog and dismiss it to the same readable passage. Normal mobile finishes opening before the connection task without the prior failure notice. Reduced uses the expected readable fallback. Paired traces and screenshots show Chart receipt and Voyage progression in both settings.

continuity.observation: The return retains Follow the lanterns on the exact Journal route. The run reports equal Voyage and edition witnesses at entry, connection and return. In each paired case the two contexts have distinct surface IDs and share the same Voyage and edition, with visible post-return progression in both positive cases.

complexity.observation: The Player can open connection guidance and resume the Chronicle with two actions. Consent and optional manual entry are contained inside the dialog. Paired handoff uses an explicit offer and the adverse case preserves the sender passage after decline.

role-outcomes.observation: The context dialog tells the authorized Player to join with the same account. The paired captures show a phone companion receiving a released Chart and a sender acknowledgment. The adverse crew context shows a read-only shared view; the return switches back to personal passage content.

fallbacks.observation: The dialog offers manual code entry. Expired pairing offers recovery guidance, the offline phone retains released Chart content, and reconnect restores in-sync status. Revocation replaces the private view with reconnect guidance at the measured 4.826 s refresh. Physical scanning and gesture ergonomics were outside this capture.

findings.observation: Normal mobile shows an optional opening failure notice before and after the connection task. The reading and connection controls remain usable, and the same passage remains legible when the dialog closes.
findings.resolution: Normal mobile shows Follow the lanterns before and after the contextual connection, without the prior opening notice. The returned screenshot and WebM show focus restored to Connect another device.

composition.observation: The companion gives Journal, Guided Lens, Chart and Artifact their own workspaces within the same dark shell. A light clue card, map and artifact panel distinguish each purpose. Returned Journal keeps the passage and fixed action strip in separate areas.

hierarchy.observation: The Voyage name and Return to Chronicle precede the current purpose. Guided Lens elevates the Captain's note and offers Choose, Inspect and Place in Guided View. Chart leads with the current objective and map; Artifact leads with The brass compass.

typography.observation: The parchment titles Follow the lanterns and The brass compass use legible serif headings. Smaller companion utility copy is subordinate but readable. The mobile Guided Lens title and Voyage name wrap without losing their words, and Journal offers larger reading size.

spacing.observation: The single-column handheld panels leave space between the status, reading controls and parchment. Chart items and options follow the map; Artifact description fits beneath its image. More purposes and the return remain reachable through vertical navigation.

controls.observation: Trace activates Change companion purpose, the Lens and its Close action, Voyage Chart, More purposes, Artifact viewer, Journal companion, larger reading size and Return to Chronicle. These actions bring up the expected content in both modes on both viewports.

contrast.observation: Dark reading text stands out against parchment; white outlines mark the Lens Close control and new active purpose headings. Guided Lens disables browser AR and explains the availability of Guided View. The capture reports no serious axe finding in the journey states.

consistency.observation: Same Voyage · in sync and the persistent Voyage name are shared anchors while the body changes purpose. The Chart received in the paired journey repeats the objective and map treatment of the manually selected Chart. The original Journal title and passage persist on return.

states.observation: The screenshots show Journal, Guided Lens, Chart, Artifact and the restored Journal on both devices and motion modes. Pairing adds offline and reconnected Chart, an empty restricted display, a received crew Chart and removal of personal content on revocation.

responsive.observation: The purpose workspaces use a wide desktop panel and stacked mobile controls. The portrait captures show readable map, artifact and text without document overflow. The landscape evidence is limited to reflow and the Chart heading in the first viewport.

keyboard.observation: The contract traces use keyboard activation for each purpose transition, Guided Lens close, reading-size change and safe return in all four contexts. In the paired traces, separate device actions demonstrate the received Chart and eventual continuation.

focus.observation: The Lens Close control has a visible outline on opening. Chart and restored Journal headings show focus rings on purpose changes, orienting the Player to the new workspace. Recorded keyboard and focus checks pass for all four configurations.

feedback.observation: Keyboard selection to visible Guided Lens clue takes 92–139 ms across four single-context captures against 5,000 ms. The paired transfer gives a visible offer followed by a separate acknowledgment when the Chart opens, with 465 and 554 ms measured acceptance-to-acknowledgment.

motion.observation: Desktop and phone recordings show purpose content and a usable Journal return in both modes. The normal phone opening settles into Follow the lanterns and its Journal controls without the previous opening notice. Reduced reaches the same passage through its readable fallback. Both paired modes advance to Voyage complete.

continuity.observation: The four single-context runs retain the Voyage and immutable edition across Lens, Chart, artifact and Journal return. Paired witness records distinct surfaces of the same Voyage and edition, and the phone trace and completed state show authorized progression after return in both modes.

complexity.observation: One purpose chooser provides named, explained choices; More purposes exposes the artifact as a secondary step. The dedicated Chart and artifact panels have a single job each. Return to Chronicle carries the Player directly back to the reading task.

role-outcomes.observation: The authorized Player actually sees the released northern-light clue, the Secret Isle map objective, the brass compass and the restored passage. The paired restricted display shows the separately authorized crew Chart, and the canonical return to the personal role restores its own passage.

fallbacks.observation: Guided View presents the released clue with browser AR unavailable. Unavailable purposes leave the Journal available. Offline state retains the latest released Chart and revocation replaces the private workspace with reconnect guidance. The adverse browser witness records no private Journal requests while sharing.

findings.observation: The normal mobile return presents an optional opening failure notice despite readable Journal content, a stable current objective, and usable continuation. The reduced-motion experience explains its readable fallback without the failure wording.
findings.resolution: Normal mobile WebM and returned screenshot show the ceremony settling into the canonical Journal with Follow the lanterns, Journal tools and Continue Voyage visible. The previous opening warning is absent.

motion.observation: The current recordings show the guarded Showcase, visually selected reduced control, then Home with its heading and Explore Chronicles available from arrival. Desktop frames 103–106 and mobile frames 93–99 show this handoff and the subsequent heading focus indication.

continuity.observation: The same signed-in identity appears before opening the harness and after Return to harbor. The navigation runs directly from the Home gateway to Showcase and back without detouring through an owner pilot.

states.observation: Initial Creators, public Creator detail and returned Creators are all rendered. The detail exposes an explicit No public work yet substate beneath the public profile, rather than ending at the hero.

feedback.observation: The district reports 1 entry on this chart and the profile clearly reports No public work yet. Its text distinguishes being publicly visible from having eligible published entries.

continuity.observation: Both viewport journeys return to the original Creators district from the public detail, maintaining the account badge and the same one-entry directory. The separate browser case contains the identity and private-canary assertions.

complexity.observation: One Creator card leads to one public profile. No public work yet pairs with the direct Browse other Creators action, so the empty profile remains navigable without depending on engagement controls.
